target: W-ISOLATION L3->L5 crash containment under injected faults

nodes.title: Measured blast-radius table: healthy-request failures per injected fault, 7 fault classes x 7 substrates x 3 rates (+PHP-FPM control)
nodes.summary: Own fault-injection experiment (740 cells, 0 driver errors). Healthy failures per injected fault at 1% rate (pooled over 5 trials): PANIC: native 0.0, wasm 0.0, fork 0.0, cordon 0.007. ABORT: native(socket-activated) 9.338, native(no SA) 24.365, wasm 0.014, fork 0, cordon 0. SEGV: native 9.709 / no-SA 24.169, wasm/fork/cordon 0. LOOP: native 3.257 with throughput x0.009; wasm 0 failures but p99 x34.724, rps x0.147; fork 0, p99 x3.37, rps x0.484. OOM: native 2.797, others ~0. FDLEAK: native 68.345, cordon(no recycle) 47.426, cordon(max_requests=50) 0.02, fork 0. POISON (C8 state leak): native 96.669, cordon 86.716, wasm instance reuse 92.581, cordon-recycle 19.068, fresh wasm instance 0, fork 0. PHP-FPM 8.4 control (3 trials): 0 healthy failures for all 7 classes (segv/abort kill only the worker, memory_limit/fd/global state torn down per request). Substrates achieving PHP parity on all expressible classes: fork-per-request (7/7) and fresh Wasm instance (6/6; fd leak not expressible by an M0 guest). Native in-process: 1/7 (panic only).
nodes.specifics: Baselines (no fault, medians of 5): native p50 622us p99 1389us 22.6k rps; wasm fresh-instance p50 760 p99 1378 21.1k rps; fork-per-request p50 1890 p99 2565 8.2k rps; cordon (4 prefork workers) p50 530 p99 5623 24.1k rps; PHP-FPM p50 1690 p99 2200 9.1k rps (different handler work: crc32). Watchdogs: wasm epoch 100 ms wall, fork ITIMER_REAL 100 ms, cordon supervisor 100 ms wall kill, outer liveness 2 s no-success -> restart. Per-request caps: RLIMIT_AS 512 MiB per native process, RLIMIT_NOFILE 256, Wasm ResourceLimiter 16 MiB. Table file state/raw/round-004/04-work/analysis/blast_table.md; aggregates state/raw/round-004/04-work/analysis/agg_main.json; raw per-request logs state/raw/round-004/04-work/fi/logs/main/t<trial>-<substrate>-<fault>-<rate>.req.tsv (i, fault, start_us, end_us, err) + .srv.log; summary rows state/raw/round-004/04-work/fi/logs/main/results.jsonl; PHP state/raw/round-004/04-work/php/logs/. Harness source state/raw/round-004/04-work/fi (finat, fiwasm, guest, fidriver), binaries+sha256 state/raw/round-004/04-work/bin. Hardware/conditions: i9-14900HX laptop, Linux 6.17.0-14, server taskset to 1 core (core 2), clients on cores 4-7, closed loop conc 16, n=3000/trial, 5 interleaved trials (shuffled order per trial), Wasmtime 48.0.7, rustc 1.98; machine shared with other research loops (loadavg 7-350 during trials; recorded per cell). Numbers tagged MEASURED.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Toy handler (~30us CPU) and Unix-socket transport; real handlers with large heaps change fork cost and OOM timing. Latency columns are contaminated by external load on a shared laptop (only counts are robust). Per-fault blast saturates at high rates for leak classes (use healthy_fail_rate there). One machine, one kernel.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Zero-blast results for wasm/fork are exact counts over 148-759 injected faults per cell; the qualitative ordering (native 1/7, cordon 3/7, cordon-recycle ~5/7, wasm-fresh 6/6, fork 7/7, PHP 7/7) is unlikely to change with hardware.

nodes.title: PHP-FPM measured control: 0 healthy failures per fault across 7 fault classes; the 'PHP miracle' quantified
nodes.summary: php:8.4-fpm-alpine (89.7 MB image), pm=static 4 workers, request_terminate_timeout=1s, memory_limit=64M, pinned to 1 core, 1 GiB, 3 interleaved trials, n=2000 (loop n=600). Healthy failures: 0 for panic(uncaught exception), abort, segv, loop, oom, fdleak, poison at 1% and 5%. Costs: segv/abort p99 x1.3-2.0, rps x0.75-0.92 at 1-5%; oom (memory_limit) p99 x8.9-17.9, rps x0.44-0.15; loop p99 1.03 s (seconds-granularity terminate timeout), rps x0.025 at 1%. Container memory 11.2 MiB for master+4 workers. Mechanism: per-request teardown in the language runtime (resources closed, globals reset, memory_limit soft cap) plus process kill for signals.
nodes.specifics: Raw: state/raw/round-004/04-work/php/logs/*.req.tsv, results.jsonl, *.srv.log (FPM logs show "execution timed out ... terminating" and "exited on signal 11"). Driver: state/raw/round-004/04-work/php/fcgi_driver.py (own minimal FastCGI client). Core dumps disabled with --ulimit core=1:1 (see coredump node); with Ubuntu apport pipe segv p99 was 104 ms in smoke run. MEASURED.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Different handler work (crc32 in PHP vs FNV loop); PHP extensions in C (not exercised) would turn segv-in-extension into worker loss same as here, and APCu/opcache shared memory would reintroduce cross-request state.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Prior map node said no public quantified data existed; this is now a measured existence proof that the PHP model reaches 0 blast for all 7 classes at ~1.7 ms p50 on one core.

nodes.title: Crash recovery is dominated by the core-dump pipeline: apport pipe + core_pipe_limit makes every crashing worker hang ~100 ms; RLIMIT_CORE=0 does not help
nodes.summary: Measured: with Ubuntu default core_pattern (|/usr/share/apport/apport ...) and core_pipe_limit=10, each SIGSEGV/SIGABRT worker stayed alive ~100 ms (cordon watchdog SIGKILLed 67/68 crashed workers, status=9); cordon p99 104 ms and capacity loss 1/4 per crash; PHP-FPM segv p99 104 ms. man core(5): RLIMIT_CORE is not enforced for piped dumps, and with core_pipe_limit>0 the kernel waits for the helper. Fix measured: prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE,0) -> cordon segv p99 104 ms -> 2.4 ms, rps 555 -> 16.7k; for PHP --ulimit core=1:1 (RLIMIT_CORE=1 pipe special case) -> p99 104 -> 4.7 ms.
nodes.specifics: L5 invariant: every crash-contained worker/child/sandbox process MUST set PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 (also blocks ptrace and makes /proc/<pid> root-owned) or RLIMIT_CORE=1, and the golden systemd unit sets LimitCORE=1 or the host disables apport; CI gate checks crash recovery p99 < 5 ms. Logs: state/raw/round-004/04-work/fi/logs/dbg/, smoke3/. MEASURED.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Hang length depends on distro helper (apport/systemd-coredump) and load; servers on hosts without a pipe helper do not see it.
nodes.underclaim_risk: This single default silently converts zero-blast substrates into 25%-capacity-loss-per-crash substrates and also feeds a crash-oracle attacker a fresh timing channel.

nodes.title: Supervisor-held listening socket (socket activation) cuts in-process crash blast radius 2-2.6x; restart (exec+init) p50 1.3-1.9 ms
nodes.summary: Native in-process server crash (abort/segv): healthy failures per crash 9.338-9.709 when the supervisor holds the listening socket and passes it as fd 3, vs 24.365-24.169 when the server binds its own socket (1% rate); at 0.1%: 10.5-12.3 vs 31.3-32.3. Failures are the in-flight + already-accepted requests (EOF), not refused connects. Restart-to-first-success p50 1.3-1.9 ms.
nodes.specifics: Mechanism: connections queue in the kernel backlog while the server is down (0pointer: 'If a service dies its listening socket stays around'). Residual = requests accepted into the in-process queue; bound it by accepting only when a worker is idle. MEASURED (fi/logs/main/*native*).
nodes.overclaim_risk: Unix-socket backlog; TCP behaviour similar but SYN backlog limits differ.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Cheap mechanism that also enables zero-downtime upgrade.

nodes.title: Resource-leak faults are gray failures: liveness watchdogs never fire, the server degrades instead of crashing
nodes.summary: fd leak (64 fds/fault, RLIMIT_NOFILE 256): native in-process 68.345 healthy failures per fault, throughput x0.073, p99 x16.553, almost no restarts (accept/open EMFILE but some requests still succeed, so the 2 s no-success liveness check never trips). Cordon without recycle 47.426/fault; with max_requests=50 0.02; fork 0; PHP 0.
nodes.specifics: L5: per-request resource ledger (fds, sockets, DB conns) released at request end by the substrate, not the handler; worker recycle (max_requests or RSS/fd high-water mark, FPM pm.max_requests / Apache MaxConnectionsPerChild / uWSGI reload-on-rss analogs) as backstop; health check must be a success-RATE SLO, not a binary liveness probe. MEASURED.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Leak size per fault chosen to bite fast.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Same pattern applies to DB connection leaks (ac.principle-cancel-equals-crash).

nodes.title: Cross-request state poisoning (C8) measured: reuse of any long-lived context leaks to ~all later requests; recycle only bounds it
nodes.summary: One poisoning request corrupts later responses: native 820.333 wrong answers per poisoning at 0.1% (until restart, i.e. forever), cordon 241.833, Wasm instance reuse 382.833, cordon with max_requests=50 24.75 (~half the recycle window x workers), fresh Wasm instance per request 0 (1 stray failure in 5 trials), fork 0, PHP 0. This is also the primitive behind cross-user data leaks (a global cache keyed without principal).
nodes.specifics: Industry convergence (fetched): Fastly Compute starts a fresh sandbox per request by default and warns that with reusable sandboxes "global variables may persist"; wasmtime serve defaults max_instance_reuse_count 1 for WASIp2 but 128 (and 16 concurrent) for WASIp3; Wasmtime maintainers called new reset paths "a big hazard ... anything gotten wrong is a CVE" (#14313). GHSA-6wgr-89rj-399p (2026-04-09) is a real pooling-allocator cross-instance linear-memory leak in specific configs. MEASURED + B sources.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Poison here is deliberate; accidental poisoning rates in real code unknown.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Wrong answers are silent (no error status), so production monitoring would not see them.

nodes.title: On 1 vCPU every runaway (loop/OOM) costs its full timeout in CPU; pool-bounded substrates add head-of-line blocking
nodes.summary: loop at 1%: throughput x0.484 fork, x0.147 wasm (4-thread pool, 100 ms epoch), x0.171 cordon (4 workers), x0.009 native (threads lost until 2 s watchdog), PHP x0.025 (1 s granularity). p99 x3.37 fork vs x34.724 wasm: fork has no pool bound so healthy requests only share CPU, while a looping guest pins 1 of 4 pool slots for 100 ms. OOM similar: wasm 16 MiB limiter fails fast (p99 x5.228), cordon touching 512 MiB p99 x9.963.
nodes.specifics: Expected CPU loss per second = fault_rate x rps x timeout. At 100 rps and 0.1% runaway with 100 ms timeout: 1% of a core; with 1 s (PHP granularity): 10%. L5: per-request CPU budget enforced by deterministic fuel (Wasmtime consume_fuel; docs: epoch is non-deterministic, fuel deterministic) or CPU-time timers (ITIMER_PROF/RLIMIT_CPU), default 10-50 ms for P2; pool size >= 4x expected runaway concurrency; memory cap fail-fast (small per-request limit) rather than large RLIMIT_AS. MEASURED.
nodes.overclaim_risk: External load inflated latency in trial 2.
nodes.underclaim_risk: An attacker can trigger runaways deliberately; this is the cost model for CPU-exhaustion DoS (bridge to W-ABUSE budgets).

nodes.title: Zero-blast fork/prefork substrates are crash oracles: respawn-without-exec keeps the address layout, enabling BROP-style probing (~4,000 requests)
nodes.summary: Blind ROP (Bittau et al., IEEE S&P 2014) needs a server that restarts after a crash with the same memory layout; nginx 1.4.0 and MySQL were exploited in ~4,000 requests within minutes. Fork-without-exec makes ASLR ineffective (Baumann et al., HotOS'19 'A fork() in the road'); Android zygote weakens ASLR for every app (Lee et al., 'From Zygote to Morula'; Morula pre-exec pool costs ~13 MB/app). nginx master respawns workers by fork. PHP-FPM's emergency_restart_threshold reload path calls execvp (fresh layout) but defaults to 0 (off). Our measured fork/cordon substrates have 0 blast per crash, which makes each crash a free probe.
nodes.specifics: L5: (1) workers/zygotes are spawned by exec (posix_spawn/fexecve of the server binary; cost measured as server restart 1.3-1.9 ms) and re-exec the zygote every N crashes; (2) per-principal crash budget: a client/tenant whose requests crash > k in window T is shed (same accounting bucket as cancellation/Rapid-Reset, cf. ac.principle-cancel-equals-crash); (3) pool-wide escalation like FPM emergency_restart_threshold / Erlang supervisor intensity (default 1 restart per 5 s, escalate). Applies to native P1 handlers too (memory-safety bugs in unsafe deps).
nodes.overclaim_risk: BROP needs a memory-corruption bug in native code; fresh Wasm instances have no host-layout oracle unless the bug is in Wasmtime itself.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Crash-respawn oracles are a direct inversion of the blast-radius metric: the better a substrate contains crashes, the cheaper probing becomes unless crashes are rate-limited per principal.

nodes.title: Guest-triggerable host aborts: in-process Wasm inherits the native-abort blast radius at 0.7-3.9 known bugs/yr
nodes.summary: Recomputed from the 81-GHSA snapshot (re-pulled 2026-10-25, 0 new): guest-triggerable DOS-PANIC (host panic/abort) advisories: M0 (core, Cranelift x86_64) 2 in 2024-26 = 0.71/yr [0.08,2.57]; M1 (+P2 components, non-fs WASI, wasi-http) 11 in 2024-26 = 3.91/yr [1.95,6.99], 2026 alone 8.6/yr. Example GHSA-q8hx-mm92-4wvg (2024-10-09): tail calls + stack traces -> "deterministic process abort" with Rust >=1.81; GHSA-75hq-h6g9-h4q5 (2024-04-02) host panic from dropped externref segment. Each such bug turns a contained trap into a whole-process crash, i.e. the measured native abort row (9.3/fault with socket activation, 24/fault without) for every concurrent request in that process.
nodes.specifics: Script state/raw/round-004/04-work/adv/recompute.py, output recomputed_rates.json; current list adv_now.tsv. Implication: the Wasm host process must itself be a supervised, socket-activated cordon with per-tenant scope, and panic=unwind does not save it (abort paths). RECOMPUTED.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Hand classification from r2 (+-3-5 advisories); 2026 surge reflects the LLM audit sprint, not necessarily a stationary rate.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Measured in-process blast results for wasm (0/fault) silently assume no such bug; this is the term that makes them non-zero.

nodes.title: M0 Wasmtime escape rate with explicit denominators: 2.21/yr long-run, 0.36/yr 2024-26, 1.23/yr 2026
nodes.summary: Exploitable sandbox escapes (impact ESC, guest-triggerable, not embedder-only) hitting M0: 12 in 2021-05-21..2026-10-25 (5.43 y) = 2.21/yr, Poisson 95% [1.14,3.86]; 1 in 2024-01-01..2026-10-25 (2.81 y) = 0.36/yr [0.00,1.98] (GHSA-897f-g5gm-fmxm, 2026-10-19); 2026 YTD 1 in 0.81 y = 1.23/yr [0.02,6.84]. M1 adds GHSA-394w, GHSA-hx6p (2024-26: 3 = 1.07/yr [0.21,3.11]); M2 (+wasi-fs) 5 = 1.78/yr. Info-leak class M0: GHSA-6wgr (pooling, config-dependent). The r3 band 0.36-2.0/yr is confirmed except the long-run end is 2.21/yr when the window starts at the first advisory (5.43 y, not 5.8 y).
nodes.specifics: Denominator choice matters 6x; use 2.21/yr as the planning rate (conservative, includes the 2021-23 reftypes/SIMD era) and 0.36/yr as the optimistic bound. RECOMPUTED from round-002 07-data/classified.json.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Published advisories only; the classification is one explorer's.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Unknown 0-days not counted; LLM-assisted auditing raised 2026 discovery rate.

nodes.title: kernelCTF LPE exploits 2023-26: 72% need user namespaces; all 111 need a syscall/socket family a tight worker allowlist denies
nodes.summary: google/security-research pocs/linux/kernelctf metadata (138 entries, 111 unique CVEs; by CVE year 2023 37, 2024 33, 2025 27, 2026 13 => ~33 exploited LPEs/yr against hardened kernels): 80 (72%) require userns; the 31 without userns need CONFIG_TLS/kTLS ULP via setsockopt (11), BPF (7), AF_UNIX GC/OOB (4: CVE-2023-4622, CVE-2024-36972, CVE-2025-40214, CVE-2026-53361), io_uring (3), perf_event_open (3), AF_ALG crypto sockets (3), vsock (1), net_sched (1). A worker filter with no socket/socketpair/setsockopt/sendmsg/recvmsg/bpf/perf_event_open/io_uring_*, clone flags filtered (no CLONE_NEWUSER), clone3 -> ENOSYS, blocks all 111 by syscall reachability (own mapping). Edera (2020-25): 42 userns-gated CVEs, nf_tables 43%.
nodes.specifics: Residual planning rate for kernel LPE reachable through such an allowlist: point 0.17/yr (basic-syscall LPEs 2014-26: futex CVE-2014-3153, StackRot CVE-2023-3269 class), rule-of-three upper 0.88/yr (0 of 111 in ~3.4 y). Bridge to W-TRANSPORT: kTLS (CONFIG_TLS) is the single largest non-userns kernelCTF surface (11), so kTLS offload must never be reachable from sandboxed workers. Data state/raw/round-004/04-work/kctf/ (metadata json + summary.txt). RECOMPUTED.
nodes.overclaim_risk: kernelCTF is bounty-selected (favours exploitable, reachable bugs); reachability mapping is mine from kernel_config fields, not per-exploit syscall traces.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Shows the OS sandbox is not a weak layer when the allowlist is tight; most kernel LPE volume is behind userns and exotic socket families.

nodes.title: Expected-loss ranking for P2 (agent-generated) code: Wasm alone ~ fork-native >> Wasm inside an OS sandbox (one order of magnitude)
nodes.summary: MODELLED, n-day attacker. Persistent attacker P(>=1 exploitable window/yr) = 1-exp(-lambda): Wasm-in-process alone (M0) 30-89%; fork-per-request native with seccomp+Landlock allowlist (kernel 0.17-0.88/yr) 16-59%; Wasm escape AND kernel LPE chained (Wasm in a sandboxed cordon or Wasm inside a fork child) 0.25-10.6% (Wasm patch lag 1-7 d, kernel 14 d; 60 d kernel lag -> 1.0-30%). Opportunistic exposure fraction F=lambda*L/365: 0.10-4.2% / 0.65-3.4% / 0.0006-0.14%. Answer to the brief: yes, an OS sandbox around Wasm changes the ranking: Wasm alone ranks last or tied with fork-native; Wasm+OS sandbox ranks first. But inside one cordon, requests of different principals are separated only by Wasm, so cross-principal risk inside a shared cordon equals the Wasm-alone row.
nodes.specifics: Script state/raw/round-004/04-work/analysis/expected_loss.py -> expected_loss.json. Cost side (MEASURED): fork-per-request p50 1.89 ms vs fresh Wasm 0.76 ms, 8.2k vs 21.1k rps on 1 core; crash containment equal (both 0 blast); fork also contains fd-leak class. Hence P2 golden = Wasm-per-request inside a per-tenant sandboxed cordon; P2 handling cross-principal data in one cordon = Wasm-in-fork or per-principal cordon.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Independence of Wasm and kernel bug arrival assumed; 0-day attackers not modelled (they defeat single layers outright); rates from small counts.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Patch lag for the Wasm layer is under our control (Cloudflare reports <24 h for V8); at 1-day lag even Wasm alone has F=0.1-0.6%.

nodes.title: Provenance -> substrate decision table with measured inputs and reversal conditions (amends R-ISO-1)
nodes.summary: P1 first-party (verified, no unsafe in handler crates): native in-process + catch_unwind + per-request arena/ledger + socket-activated supervised process + per-principal crash budget; measured blast: panic 0, oom/abort/segv 2.5-9.7 per fault, fdleak/poison unbounded -> REQUIRE per-request resource ledger and no mutable globals (lint: no static mut/OnceCell-with-interior-mutability in handler crates). P2 agent-generated / prompt-injectable: fresh Wasm instance per request (M0 config, max reuse 1, fuel 10-50 ms, 16 MiB) inside a per-tenant cordon process under seccomp+Landlock, PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0, socket activation, exec-spawned; measured blast 0 for 6/6 classes, p50 0.76 ms; residual = host-abort bugs (0.7-3.9/yr) and Wasm escape within the cordon. P2 handling cross-principal data in one cordon, or needing native libraries: fork-per-request from an exec-spawned zygote (+ optional Wasm inside) under seccomp/Landlock with clone-flag filter; blast 0 for 7/7, p50 1.9 ms, 8.2k rps/core. P3 multi-tenant third party: per-tenant cordon processes (exec-spawned) + Wasm, or microVM (Firecracker <=125 ms boot, <=5 MiB VMM overhead, cited) when native. P4 arbitrary native code: microVM/gVisor only.
nodes.specifics: REVERSAL CONDITIONS: (R1) if M0 Wasmtime exploitable escapes exceed 3/yr for two consecutive years, or our Wasmtime patch lag cannot be held <=7 d, move P2 to fork-per-request(+Wasm) by default. (R2) if a kernel LPE reachable through the worker allowlist appears (any kernelCTF entry needing only the allowed syscalls), add a microVM tier for P3 and re-audit the allowlist. (R3) if per-request fork p50 overhead on target hardware falls below 0.3 ms (e.g. lean zygote, CLONE_INTO_CGROUP spawn) the P2 default flips to fork+Wasm. (R4) if Wasmtime ships a first-class audited Instance::reset, instance reuse may be allowed for P2 only with a CI poison test passing. (R5) if P1 handlers cannot be kept free of mutable globals/unsafe, P1 moves to cordon-recycle (max_requests) or fresh Wasm. Measured density at 1 GiB (toy handler floor, MEASURED+r2): fresh Wasm instances ~19.9k (52 KB/instance component, r2) capped by ~31k VA slots of 4 GiB+32 MiB guard; fork children ~5-10k concurrent (0.1-0.2 MB each); cordon workers ~1,000 (1.0 MB RSS each, here); PHP-FPM ~2.8 MiB per worker (11.2 MiB for master+4). Extends isolation-decision-table-by-provenance (r1, E) with A/B inputs.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Decision mixes measured containment with modelled breach rates (E); one hardware platform.
nodes.underclaim_risk: R-ISO-1 direction survives, but with two binding amendments it lacked: per-tenant cordon scope and the crash-oracle/coredump/socket-activation controls.

nodes.title: Isolation fault-injection harness spec usable as a CI gate (acceptance thresholds per fault class and provenance tier)
nodes.summary: Harness: closed-loop client + supervisor that owns the listening socket; server pinned to 1 CPU (taskset) with loadavg recorded; fault taxonomy {panic, abort, segv, loop, oom, fdleak, poison} injected by a deterministic seeded selector at {0.1%, 1%, 5%}; >=5 interleaved trials, n>=3000, conc 16; per-request log (i, fault, start_us, end_us, err in {ok, connect, write, EOF, timeout, wrong-answer}); oracle = handler output recomputed by the client (detects silent poisoning). ACCEPTANCE (golden, P2 and P3 tiers): healthy failures per injected fault <= 0.05 for every class at 1% (pooled over trials, crash-attributable errors only: connect/EOF/wrong; timeouts reported separately); wrong answers == 0; p99 inflation <= 1.5x for panic/abort/segv/poison and <= 5x for loop/oom with the configured CPU budget; throughput >= 0.5x baseline at 1% loop with budget 10 ms; crash recovery p99 <= 5 ms (dumpable off); cross-request poison count == 0. P1 tier: panic blast == 0; abort/segv blast <= 12 per fault (socket activation mandatory); fdleak/poison must be 0 via the ledger/no-global lints, else fail.
nodes.specifics: Reference implementation and numbers: state/raw/round-004/04-work/fi (Rust, ~600 LOC: finat native/fork/cordon, fiwasm Wasmtime 48.0.7, fidriver), runner scripts/run_matrix.py + run_all.sh (heavy.sh), aggregation analysis/aggregate.py. Measured pass/fail today: fork PASS all; fresh-Wasm PASS all expressible (fdleak N/A) except loop p99 (x35 at 100 ms epoch: needs 10 ms fuel budget or bigger pool); cordon FAIL fdleak/poison without recycle; native FAIL abort/segv/loop/oom/fdleak/poison for P2. Seccomp gap found while building the harness: allowing clone/clone3 unfiltered in a zygote filter lets children create user namespaces (72% of kernelCTF exploits need userns) -> gate also runs a negative test: child attempting clone(CLONE_NEWUSER), socket(AF_INET), setsockopt(TCP_ULP), bpf, io_uring_setup must be killed/ENOSYS.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Thresholds are set from one machine; CI runners are noisy (use counts, not latency, as hard gates).
nodes.underclaim_risk: Same harness doubles as a regression test for Wasmtime upgrades (host-abort bugs show up as abort-class blast).

nodes.title: wasmtime serve defaults to instance reuse for WASIp3 (128 serial / 16 concurrent); a trap then hits unrelated requests
nodes.summary: src/commands/serve.rs: max_instance_reuse_count defaults to 1 for WASIp2 and 128 for WASIp3; max_instance_concurrent_reuse_count 1 / 16. PR #11807 (merged 2025-10-20) lists the disadvantage verbatim: "the blast radius of bugs in the guest is larger; a trap can affect unrelated requests, and a security flaw could leak state across requests." Issue #14313 (closed 2026-09): user-side reset 2.5-5.5x calls/s vs reinstantiate for 256 KiB guests (crossover ~0.5 MiB), maintainer refused new reset paths as CVE hazard. Our measurement: instance reuse leaks poisoned state to 93/fault at 1%.
nodes.specifics: Golden pin: if wasi-http/P3 hosting is ever enabled, pass --max-instance-reuse-count 1 and --max-instance-concurrent-reuse-count 1 (or embedder equivalent) and gate with the poison test. Fastly reusable sandboxes are likewise opt-in.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Only matters if WASIp3/serve is used.
nodes.underclaim_risk: A default flip in a future release would silently change isolation semantics; pin explicitly.

nodes.title: V8 isolate OOM is process-fatal unless the embedder handles NearHeapLimitCallback; isolate density does not imply OOM containment
nodes.summary: v8-isolate.h (ResourceConstraints): if GCs do not help and the NearHeapLimitCallback does not raise the limit, "V8 will crash with V8::FatalProcessOutOfMemory". Node workers return +16 MB and exit only the worker; Supabase edge-runtime terminates the isolate via the callback. workerd handling not verified (code search found none in jsg/io paths). Contrast with measured Wasm: 16 MiB limiter -> memory.grow returns -1 -> guest traps, 0 blast.
nodes.specifics: If a V8 substrate is ever considered (optional d), its blast-radius row for OOM equals the native abort row unless per-isolate near-heap handling is proven by the CI gate.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Production platforms (Cloudflare) clearly handle this; claim is about default embedder behaviour.

nodes.title: Skeptic of process-per-request: fork is slow, unscalable and insecure by default (HotOS'19), but measured cost at a lean zygote is 1.1-1.3 ms/request on 1 core
nodes.summary: Baumann, Appavoo, Krieger, Roscoe, 'A fork() in the road' (HotOS 2019): fork+exec time grows with parent size, posix_spawn ~0.5 ms flat (i7-6850K), Chrome fork delays up to 100 ms, fork not thread-safe, inherits secrets/fds by default, defeats ASLR without exec. Our measurement (2 MB zygote, 1 core, 16 concurrent): fork-per-request p50 1.89 ms vs fresh Wasm 0.76 ms vs native 0.62 ms; 8.2k vs 21.1k vs 22.6k rps => ~0.08 ms of extra CPU per request at saturation, ~1.1 ms extra latency under 16-way queueing. Two-sided: the 'process per request is unaffordable' claim is false for a lean zygote at household scale (8k rps/core), and the 'fork is free' claim is false (2.6x throughput cost vs Wasm, more with large zygote heaps: r2 measured 0.7 ms fork at 64 MB, 1.5 ms at 256 MB).
nodes.specifics: Design consequence: zygote must stay lean (<10 MB private), single-threaded, secret-free (no TLS keys or DB creds mapped; pass per-request capabilities by fd), exec-spawned, and children get a second stacked seccomp filter forbidding fork/clone.

nodes.title: Crash-loop damping semantics across incumbents: FPM emergency_restart (SIGSEGV/SIGBUS ring), Erlang intensity/period 1/5 s, uWSGI min-worker-lifetime 60 s, Apache MaxConnectionsPerChild
nodes.summary: php-src fpm_children.c: on child exit by SIGSEGV or SIGBUS only, record timestamp in a ring of N; if all N within emergency_restart_interval -> whole-master reload (execvp). Defaults 0/0 (off); pm.max_requests default 0 (sample config 500); request_terminate_timeout 0. Erlang supervisor: intensity 1, period 5 s default; exceed -> terminate children and escalate. uWSGI: harakiri, max-requests, reload-on-rss, min-worker-lifetime 60 s. Apache: MaxConnectionsPerChild 0 default, documented as leak limiter. None of them is per-principal: an attacker crashing workers is indistinguishable from a bug.
nodes.specifics: L5 parameters for the golden supervisor: per-principal crash budget 3 crashes / 60 s then 429 for 10 min; pool escalation 10 crashes / 10 s -> re-exec zygote (fresh ASLR) and alert; worker recycle max_requests 1000 or fd/RSS high-water; all defaults ON (incumbents ship them OFF).
nodes.underclaim_risk: Defaults-off is itself a finding (cf. gap.insecure-defaults).

nodes.title: Zygote seccomp must filter clone flags and deny clone3; children need a stacked no-fork filter
nodes.summary: Building the harness exposed that a zygote allowlist containing clone/clone3/fork (needed to spawn children; also present in the r2 zygote recipe base list) is inherited by children, so request code can create user namespaces (CLONE_NEWUSER) - the precondition of 80/111 kernelCTF exploits. clone3 passes flags in a struct seccomp cannot inspect, so it must return ENOSYS (glibc falls back to clone). CLONE_INTO_CGROUP (Linux 5.7, clone3 only) would allow per-request memory.max cgroups but conflicts with clone3 denial in children; do it in the zygote only.
nodes.specifics: Filter for zygote: clone allowed only if (flags & (CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNS|CLONE_NEWNET|CLONE_NEWPID|CLONE_NEWIPC|CLONE_NEWUTS|CLONE_NEWCGROUP))==0; clone3 -> ERRNO(ENOSYS); unshare/setns denied. Child after fork: stack a second filter denying clone/clone3/fork/vfork/execve*/socket*/setsockopt/sendmsg/recvmsg/bpf/perf_event_open/io_uring_*/ptrace/process_vm_*. Landlock before seccomp (ordering verified in r2).
nodes.overclaim_risk: Kernel may disable unprivileged userns globally (Ubuntu AppArmor restriction), masking the gap.

notes.novelty_gate: 6 queries checked: all NOVEL (best 0.10-0.27); 8 topics checked: all NOVEL (best 0.28)
notes.machine_safety: All builds and runs under tools/heavy.sh (one at a time). Shared r2 target reused; toolchain/lock drift forced a partial wasmtime recompile (+~0.4 GB in the shared dir); my unwind profile dir and fiwasm artifacts deleted after measurement; binaries archived in 04-work/bin (14 MB). 04-work total 74 MB. Docker image php:8.4-fpm-alpine 89.7 MB. Disk free 27 GB.
notes.contamination: Laptop shared with other loops (loadavg 7-350, xtask at ~1900% CPU at times). Counts robust; latency medians noisy; trial 2 worst. Harness bug: orphaned cordon workers accumulated in trials 1-2 (idle, 0% CPU); fixed for trials 3-5.
notes.not_done: V8/deno_core substrate (d) not measured (no prebuilt <500 MB checked; time). Hyperlight/Firecracker only cited.
notes.R-ISO-1 verdict: Direction unchanged (provenance-keyed), evidence upgraded E->B for the containment inputs; amendments: per-tenant cordon scope for P2, exec-spawn + crash budget, dumpable=0, socket activation, reuse=1 pins, clone-flag filter; reversal conditions R1-R5.

protocol_implications: R-ISO-1 amend: P2 Wasm cordons are per-tenant (cross-principal data in a shared cordon -> Wasm-in-fork); reversal conditions R1-R5 attached.

New golden invariants: PR_SET_DUMPABLE=0 (or RLIMIT_CORE=1) on all crash-contained processes; supervisor-held listening socket; exec-spawned workers/zygotes; per-principal crash budget; max_instance_reuse=1; zygote clone-flag filter + stacked child filter; per-request fuel/CPU budget 10-50 ms.
Add isolation fault-injection CI gate (r4i04.isolation-fault-ci-gate) next to the storage crash gate; hard gates on counts (blast <=0.05/fault, wrong answers 0), soft gates on latency.
P1 native handlers require a per-request resource ledger and a no-mutable-global lint; otherwise measured fdleak/poison blast is unbounded.
kTLS (CONFIG_TLS) must not be reachable from sandboxed workers (11 kernelCTF LPEs) - bridge to W-TRANSPORT kTLS decision.
self_improvement: Harness pkill-by-socket-path cleanup broke under socket activation (args became fd:3) and a pkill pattern matched the agent's own shell; future harnesses should spawn servers in their own process group and kill(-pgid).
Shared-laptop contention (loadavg up to 350) makes latency gates meaningless; heavy.sh serializes only heavy jobs, not other loops. Record loadavg per cell and gate on counts.
Reusing another round's target dir still triggered a partial wasmtime rebuild because the toolchain was not recorded in a rust-toolchain file; benches should commit rust-toolchain + Cargo.lock.
